clips.send: Beyond the textbook (optional): Liu Hui’s method and the 3,072-gon, the 24,576-gon hypothesis, al-Kāshī (c. 1424), 355 over 113 in 16th-century Europe, abacus history and the “三下五去二” rule, the structure of the simplified armillary, solar longitudes of the terms and day-length maths, and the world comparison dates. All timeline dates are approximate.

clips.send: On the seismoscope: the page follows the textbook and the Later Han biography of Zhang Heng (“the dragon facing the quake drops its ball”); the internal mechanism is a modern reconstruction (Wang Zhenduo’s 1951 upright-pillar model; the 2005 suspended-pendulum model by a team of Chinese seismologists) and is still debated, matching the textbook activity asking students to compare reconstructions.

clips.send: He showed pi lies between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, and gave two fractions: 22 over 7 (the “rough ratio”) and 355 over 113 (the “close ratio”). His book is lost; historians think he may have worked up to a 24,576-sided polygon, which is what this demo does.

clips.send: Draw a hexagon inside a circle, then keep doubling the sides: 12, 24, 48… The polygon’s perimeter creeps up on the circle’s. A polygon inside gives a value below pi ; one outside gives a value above. pi is trapped in between.

clips.send: If you run out of lower beads, use “三下五去二”: push down an upper bead (+5) and take away two lower beads ( minus 2). 5 minus 2 equals 3. The Chinese idiom “three down, five off two” comes from this and means getting a job done quickly.

clips.send: 公元 138 年，洛阳城里一台铜仪器“当”的一声，一条龙吐出了铜球——可是城里谁也没觉得地在动。几天后，信使飞马赶到：几百千米外的陇西发生了地震！这台仪器就是张衡的地动仪。这一课，你要像古代科学家一样：测地震、追 派 、打算盘、看星星。
